prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2025-10-30. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 0.62 |
| Retained earnings       | 36,115M |
| Current liabilities     | 8,286M |
| Current assets          | 5,119M |
| Shareholders' equity    | -2,646M |
| Total liabilities       | 37,604M |
| Total assets            | 35,008M |
| EBIT / operating income | 3,230M |
| Revenue                 | 5,251M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2025-10-30, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The reported negative shareholders' equity indicates that total liabilities exceed total assets, producing a deeply negative tangible book value and implying balance-sheet insolvency. Combined with a current ratio of 0.62 (signaling acute liquidity pressure) and an Altman Z-score in the distress zone, these metrics place the issuer well below investment-grade and into the lower speculative-grade segment. Positive EBIT provides some offset but is insufficient to support a rating above CCC territory given the absence of any mitigating cash-flow or covenant data.
DECISION: CCC
(The final rating reflects the finest granularity justifiable from the supplied ratios alone.)
